questions.text:
प्रश्न संख्या 1 में दो कथन दिए गए हैं – जिनमें एक को अभिकथन (A) तथा दूसरे को कारण (R) द्वारा अंकित किया गया है। इन कथनों को ध्यान से पढ़िए और नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से उत्तर के रूप में सही विकल्प चुनिए :

अभिकथन (A) : भारत में पंचवर्षीय योजनाओं का विचार सोवियत संघ से प्रेरित था।
कारण (R) : तीव्र आर्थिक संकट के कारण भारत सरकार ने 1966 में 'प्लान हॉलिडे' को प्रारम्भ किया था।
questions.text_english:
Given below are two statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Read these statements and choose the correct answer from the given options :

Assertion (A) : The idea of Five Year Plans (FYP) in India was inspired by the USSR.
Reason (R) : Due to acute economic crisis, the Indian Government started 'Plan Holiday' in 1966.
questions.instruction_line: विकल्प में से सही उत्तर चुनिए
questions.instruction_line_english: Choose the correct answer from the options

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परंतु कारण (R) अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परंतु कारण (R) सही है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परंतु कारण (R) गलत है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B). Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are individually true statements. India's Five Year Plans were indeed inspired by the Soviet model of centralised planning. The Indian government did declare a Plan Holiday in 1966 due to the severe economic crisis caused by two wars (1962 and 1965) and back-to-back droughts. However, the Plan Holiday was not the reason or explanation for why India adopted Five Year Plans from the USSR — these are two separate, unconnected facts. Therefore, Reason (R) does not correctly explain Assertion (A), making option (B) correct.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) है। अभिकथन (A) सही है क्योंकि भारत में पंचवर्षीय योजनाओं की प्रेरणा वास्तव में सोवियत संघ के केंद्रीकृत नियोजन मॉडल से मिली थी। कारण (R) भी सही है क्योंकि 1966 में भारत सरकार ने आर्थिक संकट के कारण 'प्लान हॉलिडे' घोषित किया था। परंतु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता, क्योंकि दोनों कथन असंबद्ध तथ्य हैं।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सी घटना सुरक्षा की पारम्परिक धारणा से संबंधित है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following is related to the traditional notion of security ?

options.B: वैश्विक तापमान में लगातार वृद्धि होना
options.D: विश्व में कोविड-19 महामारी का फैलना

options_english.B: Continuous rise in the global temperature
options_english.D: Spread of COVID-19 epidemic in the world

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) Russia–Ukraine War. The traditional notion of security refers to threats that involve the military use of force by one state against another, including wars, border conflicts, and armed aggression between nations. The Russia–Ukraine War is a classic interstate military conflict and therefore fits the traditional notion of security. Options (B) and (D) — rising global temperatures and the COVID-19 pandemic — are non-traditional security threats as they are not caused by military force. Option (C), the 9/11 terrorist attack, is also generally classified as a non-traditional threat since it was carried out by a non-state actor.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) रूस–यूक्रेन युद्ध है। सुरक्षा की पारम्परिक धारणा में एक राज्य द्वारा दूसरे राज्य के विरुद्ध सैन्य बल का प्रयोग शामिल होता है। रूस–यूक्रेन युद्ध एक अंतर-राज्यीय सैन्य संघर्ष है। वैश्विक तापमान, COVID-19 और 9/11 का हमला अपारम्परिक खतरों की श्रेणी में आते हैं।

questions.text: प्रथम दो पंचवर्षीय योजनाओं के संबंध में निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा एक कथन असत्य है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct about the first two Five Year Plan ?

options.A: प्रथम पंचवर्षीय योजना का ड्राफ्ट के.एन. राज द्वारा और द्वितीय पंचवर्षीय योजना का ड्राफ्ट पी.सी. महालनोबिस द्वारा तैयार किया गया था।
options.B: प्रथम पंचवर्षीय योजना का फोकस कृषि और दूसरी पंचवर्षीय योजना का फोकस उद्योगों पर था।
options.C: प्रथम पंचवर्षीय योजना में सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र की सक्रिय भूमिका पर जोर दिया गया और द्वितीय पंचवर्षीय योजना में बड़े स्तर की योजनाओं के लिए भारी आबंटन किया गया।
options.D: प्रथम पंचवर्षीय योजना का उद्देश्य औद्योगिक उत्पादन में वृद्धि करना था जबकि द्वितीय पंचवर्षीय योजना में सार्वजनिक और निजी क्षेत्र के उद्योगों की सुरक्षा के लिए सरकार ने पर्याप्त शुल्क लगाया।

options_english.A: The first Five Year Plan was drafted by K.N. Raj and the second Five Year Plan was drafted by P.C. Mahalnobis.
options_english.B: The first Five Year Plan focussed on agriculture and the second Five Year Plan focussed on industries.
options_english.C: The first Five Year Plan emphasized on the active role of the public sector and the second Five Year Plan made huge allocations for large scale projects.
options_english.D: The aim of first Five Year Plan was to raise the industrial production and in the second Five Year Plan, the government imposed substantial tariffs on imports in order to protect both public and private sector industries.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (D). This statement is NOT correct. The First Five Year Plan (1951–56) focused primarily on agriculture, rehabilitation, and addressing food shortages — not on raising industrial production. It was the Second Five Year Plan (1956–61), drafted by P.C. Mahalanobis, that focused on heavy industries and rapid industrialisation. The imposition of tariffs to protect industries was a feature of the Second Plan, not the First. Options (A), (B), and (C) are all factually accurate statements about the two plans.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) है। यह कथन असत्य है। प्रथम पंचवर्षीय योजना का मुख्य उद्देश्य कृषि और खाद्य उत्पादन में सुधार करना था, न कि औद्योगिक उत्पादन में वृद्धि। भारी उद्योगों और आयात शुल्क की नीति द्वितीय पंचवर्षीय योजना से संबंधित थी।

questions.text: बाल्टिक गणराज्यों की सही तिकड़ी (तीन राज्यों) की पहचान कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Identify the correct trio of Baltic Republics :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania. The three Baltic Republics — Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania — are located on the eastern coast of the Baltic Sea. They were formerly part of the Soviet Union and declared independence in 1990–91, becoming the first Soviet republics to do so. Slovenia and Romania are not Baltic states; Slovenia is in Central Europe and Romania is in South-Eastern Europe. Options (B), (C), and (D) incorrectly include Slovenia and Romania, which are not Baltic Republics.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) एस्टोनिया, लताविया, लिथुआनिया है। ये तीन देश बाल्टिक सागर के पूर्वी तट पर स्थित हैं और पूर्व सोवियत संघ का हिस्सा थे। स्लोवानिया और रोमानिया बाल्टिक गणराज्य नहीं हैं।

questions.text:
नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं :
कथन I : अंतर्राष्ट्रीय मुद्रा कोष (आई एम एफ) एक ऐसा अंतर्राष्ट्रीय संगठन है जो अंतर्राष्ट्रीय स्तर की वित्तीय संस्थाओं और नियमों की देखरेख करता है।
कथन II : अंतर्राष्ट्रीय मुद्रा कोष संगठन में सभी 189 सदस्यों को एक समान अधिकार और दर्जा प्राप्त है।
उपर्युक्त कथनों के संदर्भ में नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए :
questions.text_english:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : The International Monetary Fund (IMF) is an international organization that oversees those financial institutions and regulations that act at the international level.
Statement II : All the 189 members of IMF organization have equal say.
In the light of above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

options.A: कथन I और कथन II दोनों सत्य हैं।
options.B: कथन I और कथन II दोनों असत्य हैं।
options.C: कथन I सत्य है, परंतु कथन II असत्य है।
options.D: कथन I असत्य है, परंतु कथन II सत्य है।

options_english.A: Both statement I and statement II are true.
options_english.B: Both statement I and statement II are false.
options_english.C: Statement I is true, but statement II is false.
options_english.D: Statement I is false, but statement II is true.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C). Statement I is true — the IMF is indeed an international organisation that oversees global financial institutions and regulations to ensure international monetary stability. Statement II is false — not all 189 members of the IMF have equal say. The IMF operates on a quota-based voting system where wealthier and economically more powerful nations like the United States have significantly more voting power than smaller or developing nations. This unequal representation is one of the major criticisms of the IMF. Hence, Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) है। कथन I सत्य है — IMF अंतर्राष्ट्रीय वित्तीय संस्थाओं की देखरेख करता है। कथन II असत्य है — IMF में सभी सदस्यों को समान मताधिकार नहीं मिलता; यह कोटा प्रणाली पर आधारित है जिसमें अमीर देशों का अधिक प्रभाव होता है।

questions.text: 'सहयोग मूलक सुरक्षा' की अवधारणा के संबंध में निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन सत्य है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following statements is True about the concept of 'Co-operative Security' ?

options.A: विश्व के शक्तिशाली देशों द्वारा गैर-पारम्परिक खतरों के विरुद्ध सैन्य कार्यवाही करना।
options.B: 'नाटो' देशों के द्वारा खतरे की स्थिति में 'सामूहिक सुरक्षा' को सुनिश्चित करना।
options.C: एक राज्य के अन्दर विभिन्न माध्यमों से आंतरिक सुरक्षा को मजबूत करना।
options.D: विश्व के कई देशों के द्वारा गैर-पारम्परिक खतरों का मिल-जुल कर समाधान निकालना।

options_english.A: Initiating action by the developed countries against non-traditional threats.
options_english.B: Ensuring 'collective security' by the NATO countries in case of threats.
options_english.C: Strengthening internal security by various measures within a state.
options_english.D: Involving several countries to decide on a collective solution against non-traditional threats.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (D). Co-operative Security is a concept where multiple countries come together to collectively address and find solutions to non-traditional security threats such as terrorism, climate change, pandemics, and human trafficking. It is not limited to military alliances like NATO (ruling out option B), nor is it the sole action of powerful/developed nations (ruling out option A), nor does it refer to internal security measures of a single state (ruling out option C). The defining feature of cooperative security is broad multilateral participation to tackle shared threats.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) है। सहयोग मूलक सुरक्षा में विश्व के कई देश मिलकर गैर-पारम्परिक खतरों जैसे आतंकवाद, जलवायु परिवर्तन आदि का समाधान निकालते हैं। यह केवल नाटो तक सीमित नहीं है और न ही यह किसी एक राज्य की आंतरिक सुरक्षा से संबंधित है।
questions.chapter: समकालीन विश्व में सुरक्षा / Security in the Contemporary World

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन 'वीटो शक्ति' की सर्वश्रेष्ठ व्याख्या है ?
questions.text_english: Which statement is the best description of 'Veto Power' ?

options.A: यह सकारात्मक मतदान की शक्ति है।
options.B: दूसरे विश्व युद्ध के बाद केवल संयुक्त राष्ट्र सुरक्षा परिषद् के स्थायी सदस्यों को विश्व में शांति स्थापना के लिए, वीटो शक्ति दी गयी।
options.C: संयुक्त राष्ट्र सुरक्षा परिषद् के समस्त अस्थायी सदस्यों को केवल दो वर्ष तक वीटो शक्ति प्रयोग करने का अधिकार है।
options.D: संयुक्त राष्ट्र सुरक्षा परिषद् के सभी सदस्यों को वीटो शक्ति प्राप्त है।

options_english.A: It is a power of positive voting.
options_english.B: After the end of the Second World War, Veto Power is given only to permanent members of the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) to establish peace in the world.
options_english.C: All the temporary members of the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) have the right to use Veto Power only for two years.
options_english.D: All the members of the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) possess Veto Power.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B). Veto Power was granted after World War II exclusively to the five permanent members (P5) of the UN Security Council — the USA, UK, France, Russia, and China — to maintain international peace and security. It gives any one of these members the authority to block (veto) any substantive resolution. Option (A) is wrong because veto is the power to reject or block, not affirm. Option (C) is wrong because temporary/non-permanent members do not have veto power at all. Option (D) is wrong because not all UNSC members possess veto power.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) है। वीटो शक्ति द्वितीय विश्व युद्ध के बाद संयुक्त राष्ट्र सुरक्षा परिषद् के पाँच स्थायी सदस्यों — अमरीका, ब्रिटेन, फ्रांस, रूस और चीन — को दी गई। अस्थायी सदस्यों को यह शक्ति प्राप्त नहीं है।
questions.chapter: संयुक्त राष्ट्र और उसके संगठन / United Nations and its Organisations

questions.text: मई 1991 के अपने चुनाव अभियान में राजीव गाँधी का अन्तिम दौरा किस राज्य में था ?
questions.text_english: Which was the last state toured by Rajiv Gandhi for his election campaign in May 1991 ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) Tamil Nadu. Rajiv Gandhi was assassinated on 21 May 1991 at Sriperumbudur in Tamil Nadu during an election rally, making it the last state he visited during his 1991 election campaign. He was killed in a suicide bomb attack carried out by the LTTE (Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam). Options (B) Karnataka, (C) Kerala, and (D) Andhra Pradesh are all incorrect as the fatal campaign visit ended in Tamil Nadu.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) तमिलनाडु है। राजीव गाँधी की 21 मई 1991 को तमिलनाडु के श्रीपेरम्बुदूर में चुनाव रैली के दौरान LTTE द्वारा हत्या की गई थी। यही उनका अंतिम चुनावी दौरा था।
questions.chapter: एक दल के प्रभुत्व का दौर / Era of One-Party Dominance

questions.text:
सूची-I का सूची-II से सही मिलान कीजिए और दिए गए कोड से उत्तर का सही विकल्प चुनिए :
सूची-I: (a) कांग्रेस फॉर डेमोक्रेसी, (b) गरीबी हटाओ, (c) मोरारजी देसाई के नेतृत्व में छात्र आंदोलन, (d) सम्पूर्ण क्रांति
सूची-II: (i) गुजरात, (ii) जयप्रकाश नारायण, (iii) जगजीवन राम, (iv) इंदिरा गाँधी
questions.text_english:
Match List-I with List-II correctly and choose the correct answer from the codes given below :
List-I: (a) Congress for democracy, (b) Garibi Hatao, (c) Student movement led by Morarji Desai, (d) Total Revolution
List-II: (i) Gujarat, (ii) Jay Prakash Narayan, (iii) Jagjeevan Ram, (iv) Indira Gandhi
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C): (a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(ii). Congress for Democracy was formed by Jagjeevan Ram (iii) who broke away from the Congress party before the 1977 elections. The 'Garibi Hatao' slogan was given by Indira Gandhi (iv) during the 1971 general elections. The student movement in Gujarat was led by students against the government of Chimanbhai Patel and is associated with Gujarat (i), where Morarji Desai supported protesters. The Total Revolution call was given by Jayaprakash Narayan (ii) in Bihar in 1974. Therefore, option (C) is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) है। कांग्रेस फॉर डेमोक्रेसी — जगजीवन राम, गरीबी हटाओ — इंदिरा गाँधी, मोरारजी देसाई के नेतृत्व में छात्र आंदोलन — गुजरात, सम्पूर्ण क्रांति — जयप्रकाश नारायण।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन 'शाक थेरेपी' का परिणाम नहीं है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following is NOT a consequence of 'Shock Therapy' ?

options.A: रूसी मुद्रा रुबल के मूल्य में गिरावट आई।
options.B: पूरे क्षेत्र की अर्थव्यवस्था तहस-नहस हो गई।
options.C: समाज कल्याण की व्यवस्था में मजबूती आ गई।
options.D: सामूहिक 'फार्म' की व्यवस्था भंग हो गई।

options_english.A: The value of the Rouble, the Russian currency declined.
options_english.B: The economy of the entire region was ruined.
options_english.C: The system of social welfare got strengthened.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C). The strengthening of the social welfare system was NOT a consequence of Shock Therapy. In fact, the opposite happened — the social welfare systems that existed under the Soviet Union collapsed after Shock Therapy was applied in Russia and other post-communist states. Shock Therapy caused the Russian Rouble to crash (A), devastated the economies of the entire region (B), and led to the disintegration of the collective farm system (D). These are all documented negative consequences of the rapid and drastic shift to a market economy.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) है। 'शाक थेरेपी' का परिणाम समाज कल्याण व्यवस्था में मजबूती नहीं बल्कि उसका पतन था। शाक थेरेपी के कारण रूस की अर्थव्यवस्था चरमरा गई, रुबल का मूल्य गिरा और सामूहिक कृषि व्यवस्था ध्वस्त हुई।

(i) अन्दरूनी गड़बड़ी के आधार पर आपातकाल की घोषणा करना।
(ii) जॉर्ज फर्नांडिस के नेतृत्व में सरकारी कर्मचारियों द्वारा रेल हड़ताल करना।
(iii) भारत में छठा आम चुनाव होना।
(iv) केशवानंद भारती मामले में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय द्वारा संविधान की 'बुनियादी संरचना' की अवधारणा घोषित करना।
सही विकल्प चुनिए :
questions.text_english:
Arrange the following events in chronological order :
(i) Declaration of National Emergency on the basis of internal disturbances.
(ii) Railway strike by government employees under the leadership of George Fernandes.
(iii) Sixth General Election held in India.
(iv) Declaration of the doctrine of 'basic structure' of the Constitution in the 'Keshavananda Bharti' case by the Supreme Court.
Choose the correct option :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A): (iv), (ii), (i), (iii). The correct chronological order is: (iv) The Keshavananda Bharti judgment declaring the Basic Structure doctrine was delivered in April 1973. (ii) The All India Railway Strike led by George Fernandes took place in May 1974. (i) The National Emergency on the grounds of internal disturbances was declared on 25 June 1975. (iii) The Sixth General Election in India (the first post-Emergency election) was held in March 1977. This sequence — 1973, 1974, 1975, 1977 — matches option (A).
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) है। कालक्रम इस प्रकार है: केशवानंद भारती मामला — 1973, रेल हड़ताल — 1974, आपातकाल की घोषणा — 25 जून 1975, छठा आम चुनाव — 1977।

questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) National Democratic Alliance (NDA). The NDA, led by the BJP, has formed the central government the maximum number of times among the listed alliances. It formed governments in 1999–2004 under Atal Bihari Vajpayee, and then again in 2014–2019 and 2019–2024 under Narendra Modi, and again after 2024. Therefore, the NDA has formed the central government the most number of times.

questions.text_english: Highlight any four threats to non-traditional security.

key_points: Terrorism — cross-border and domestic attacks by non-state actors
Human trafficking and transnational crime
Environmental degradation and climate change
Pandemic diseases such as COVID-19
Poverty and food insecurity
Cyber threats and information warfare

questions.solution: Non-traditional security threats are those that go beyond conventional military attacks by states and endanger human life in other ways. Four major non-traditional security threats are: first, global terrorism carried out by non-state actors across national borders; second, environmental threats such as climate change and natural disasters that displace populations; third, the spread of pandemic diseases like COVID-19 which threaten human health on a massive scale; and fourth, human trafficking and transnational crime networks that exploit vulnerable populations.
questions.solution_hindi: अपारम्परिक सुरक्षा के चार प्रमुख खतरे हैं: (1) वैश्विक आतंकवाद — गैर-राज्य अभिकर्ताओं द्वारा सीमा पार हमले; (2) पर्यावरणीय खतरे जैसे जलवायु परिवर्तन और प्राकृतिक आपदाएँ; (3) महामारी रोग जैसे कोविड-19; (4) मानव तस्करी और अंतर्राष्ट्रीय अपराध।

questions.text_english: Assess the impact of outside powers on the South Asian Countries.

key_points: USA and China have significant strategic and economic interests in South Asia
China's growing influence through investment and the Belt and Road Initiative
USA's influence through aid, military partnerships, and trade
Outside powers complicate regional conflicts, especially India-Pakistan tensions

questions.solution: Outside powers, particularly the United States and China, have significantly influenced the politics and economies of South Asian countries. The USA has provided military and economic aid to Pakistan, affecting the regional balance of power and complicating India-Pakistan relations. China's growing influence through massive investments, the Belt and Road Initiative, and military cooperation — especially with Pakistan — has created strategic concerns for India. These external interventions often deepen existing conflicts rather than resolve them, making genuine regional cooperation under SAARC difficult.
questions.solution_hindi: दक्षिण एशिया पर अमरीका और चीन जैसी बाहरी शक्तियों का गहरा प्रभाव है। अमरीका ने पाकिस्तान को सैन्य और आर्थिक सहायता दी है जिससे भारत-पाकिस्तान संबंध प्रभावित हुए हैं। चीन ने CPEC और BRI के माध्यम से इस क्षेत्र में अपना प्रभाव बढ़ाया है जो भारत की सुरक्षा के लिए चुनौती है।

questions.text_english: How does the geographical location of the North-East region has affected the expression of its regional demands ? Explain.

key_points: The North-East is geographically isolated from mainland India, connected only by the Siliguri Corridor
Shares long international borders with China, Myanmar, Bangladesh, Bhutan and Nepal
Isolation led to feelings of neglect and demands for greater autonomy or separate statehood
Porous borders enabled cross-border insurgencies and influx of migrants, intensifying regional tensions

questions.solution: The North-East region of India is geographically isolated from the rest of the country, connected to mainland India only through the narrow Siliguri Corridor (also called the Chicken's Neck). It shares long and often porous international borders with China, Myanmar, Bangladesh, Bhutan, and Nepal. This isolation has historically led to a sense of neglect and underdevelopment, fuelling demands for greater autonomy, separate statehood, and in some cases, even secession. The porous borders have also facilitated insurgent movements and illegal migration, further intensifying regional demands and conflicts.
questions.solution_hindi: पूर्वोत्तर भारत की भौगोलिक स्थिति अनूठी है। यह क्षेत्र केवल सिलीगुड़ी कॉरिडोर (चिकन नेक) के माध्यम से मुख्य भारत से जुड़ा है। इसकी चीन, म्यांमार, बांग्लादेश, भूटान और नेपाल के साथ लम्बी अंतर्राष्ट्रीय सीमाएँ हैं। इस भौगोलिक अलगाव के कारण उपेक्षा का एहसास हुआ और अलग राज्य या स्वायत्तता की माँगें उठीं। छिद्रपूर्ण सीमाओं के कारण उग्रवाद और प्रवासियों का प्रवेश भी क्षेत्रीय माँगों को प्रभावित करता है।

questions.text: शरणार्थी और प्रवासी जन में कोई दो अंतर स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Explain any two differences between the refugees and the migrants.

key_points: Refugees flee persecution, war, or natural disaster and cannot safely return; migrants move voluntarily for economic, social, or personal reasons
Refugees are entitled to international protection under international law (UNHCR); migrants are protected by the laws of their host country
Refugees cross borders out of compulsion; migrants cross borders out of choice

questions.solution: Refugees and migrants differ in two important ways. First, refugees are forced to flee their home countries due to war, persecution, or serious human rights violations and cannot return safely, whereas migrants move voluntarily — usually in search of better economic opportunities, education, or to reunite with family. Second, refugees enjoy specific legal protections under international law through bodies like the UNHCR, while migrants are governed by the domestic immigration laws of the country they move to and do not receive the same international legal protections.
questions.solution_hindi: शरणार्थी और प्रवासी में दो प्रमुख अंतर हैं। पहला, शरणार्थी युद्ध, उत्पीड़न या मानवाधिकार उल्लंघन के कारण मजबूरी में अपना देश छोड़ते हैं, जबकि प्रवासी बेहतर आर्थिक अवसरों के लिए स्वेच्छा से दूसरे देश जाते हैं। दूसरा, शरणार्थियों को UNHCR के अंतर्राष्ट्रीय कानून के तहत संरक्षण प्राप्त है, जबकि प्रवासी केवल गंतव्य देश के घरेलू कानूनों द्वारा शासित होते हैं।

questions.text_english: Name any four political parties that had merged to form Janata Party in 1977.

key_points: Bharatiya Lok Dal
Jana Sangh
Congress (O) / Congress (Organisation)
Socialist Party
Congress for Democracy (led by Jagjeevan Ram)

questions.solution: The Janata Party was formed in 1977 by the merger of several opposition parties that united against the Emergency imposed by Indira Gandhi. Four such parties were: (1) Bharatiya Lok Dal, led by Charan Singh; (2) Jana Sangh, the right-wing Hindu nationalist party; (3) Congress (Organisation) or Congress (O), the old-guard Congress faction; and (4) Congress for Democracy, formed by Jagjeevan Ram just before the elections. The Socialist Party also merged into the Janata Party. Together they won the 1977 general elections and formed India's first non-Congress government.
questions.solution_hindi: 1977 में जनता पार्टी के गठन के लिए विलय करने वाली चार पार्टियाँ थीं: (1) भारतीय लोकदल, (2) जनसंघ, (3) कांग्रेस (ओ), (4) कांग्रेस फॉर डेमोक्रेसी (जगजीवन राम द्वारा गठित)। समाजवादी पार्टी भी इसमें शामिल हुई।

questions.text: 1989 के बाद भारत में 'गठबन्धन की सरकारों' के गठन के लिए उत्तरदायी मुख्य कारण का विश्लेषण कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Analyse the main reason responsible for the formation of Coalition Governments after 1989.

key_points: The decline of Congress's dominance and the rise of regional parties
No single party could win an absolute majority in Parliament
Rise of OBC politics, caste-based mobilisation and regional aspirations
Mandal Commission recommendations energised new political forces

questions.solution: The main reason for the formation of coalition governments in India after 1989 was the decline of the Congress Party's dominance and the simultaneous rise of strong regional parties and caste-based political movements. The implementation of the Mandal Commission Report energised backward caste politics, leading to the fragmentation of the national vote. As no single party could win an absolute majority on its own, parties were compelled to form alliances and coalitions to govern at the centre. This marked the beginning of the era of multi-party coalition politics in India.
questions.solution_hindi: 1989 के बाद गठबंधन सरकारों के गठन का मुख्य कारण कांग्रेस पार्टी के प्रभुत्व का अंत और क्षेत्रीय दलों का उदय था। मंडल आयोग की सिफारिशों से जाति आधारित राजनीति को बल मिला जिससे राष्ट्रीय मतों का विखंडन हुआ। किसी भी पार्टी को स्पष्ट बहुमत नहीं मिलने के कारण गठबंधन सरकारें बनाना अनिवार्य हो गया।

sub_questions.text_english: Explain any four differences between the governments formed in the first three General Elections held in India after independence and the coalition governments formed after the year 1989.

key_points: Single-party Congress majority vs multi-party coalition governments
Strong centralised leadership (Nehru) vs power-sharing among multiple parties
Stable governments with full term vs frequent changes and instability in coalitions
Dominant ideology (Nehruvian socialism) vs compromise-driven mixed ideological platforms

sub_questions.solution: The governments formed after the first three general elections (1952, 1957, 1962) differed from post-1989 coalition governments in four significant ways. First, the early governments were single-party majority governments led by the Congress under Jawaharlal Nehru, while post-1989 governments were multi-party coalitions requiring alliances of several parties to secure a majority. Second, the early governments had strong, unified leadership with a clear mandate, whereas coalition governments required power-sharing among partners with often divergent agendas. Third, the Congress-led governments were stable and served their full terms, while many coalition governments after 1989 were short-lived and prone to collapse. Fourth, the early governments followed a coherent Nehruvian socialist ideology, whereas coalition governments had to adopt compromise-driven platforms blending different ideological positions.

sub_questions.text: भारतीय राजनीति के संदर्भ में गठबंधन की सरकारों के किन्हीं चार लाभों की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain any four advantages of coalition governments with reference to Indian politics.

key_points: Greater representation of regional and diverse interests
Promotes power-sharing and prevents authoritarian concentration
Encourages political accommodation and consensus building
Gives voice to smaller parties and marginalised groups

sub_questions.solution: Coalition governments have offered several advantages in the context of Indian politics. First, they provide greater representation to regional parties and diverse socio-cultural groups that might otherwise be ignored by a dominant national party, making governance more inclusive. Second, coalition politics prevents the dangerous concentration of power in one party or one leader, thus strengthening democratic checks and balances. Third, they encourage political accommodation and consensus-building, as parties with different ideologies must negotiate and compromise. Fourth, smaller parties representing marginalised communities — such as Dalits, tribals, or regional minorities — gain meaningful political power and influence in policy-making within coalition arrangements.

questions.text: मिखाइल गोर्बाचेव द्वारा शुरू किए गए सुधार सोवियत संघ को विघटन से क्यों नहीं बचा पाए ? कोई दो कारण स्पष्ट कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Why could the reforms initiated by Mikhail Gorbachev not save the disintegration of Soviet Union ? Explain any two reasons.

key_points: Glasnost (openness) unleashed nationalist and separatist movements that Gorbachev could not control
Perestroika (economic restructuring) created economic chaos instead of prosperity, eroding public confidence
The democratic space created by reforms allowed anti-Soviet forces to organise and demand independence

questions.solution: Mikhail Gorbachev's reforms of Glasnost (political openness) and Perestroika (economic restructuring) were well-intentioned but ultimately accelerated the disintegration of the Soviet Union for two key reasons. First, Glasnost gave citizens the freedom to criticise the government and discuss historical grievances, which unleashed powerful nationalist and separatist movements in the republics — particularly in the Baltic states, Ukraine, and the Caucasus — that quickly went beyond what Gorbachev could control or contain. Second, Perestroika created severe economic disruption as it dismantled the old centralised command economy without establishing a functioning market economy, leading to shortages, inflation, and falling living standards that destroyed public trust in the Soviet system and in Gorbachev himself.
questions.solution_hindi: मिखाइल गोर्बाचेव के ग्लासनोस्त और पेरेस्त्रोइका सुधार दो कारणों से सोवियत संघ को बचा नहीं सके। पहला, ग्लासनोस्त ने नागरिकों को सरकार की आलोचना करने की स्वतंत्रता दी जिससे बाल्टिक राज्यों, यूक्रेन और काकेशस में राष्ट्रवादी और अलगाववादी आंदोलन भड़क उठे जिन पर गोर्बाचेव काबू नहीं कर सके। दूसरा, पेरेस्त्रोइका ने आर्थिक अव्यवस्था पैदा की, जिससे कमी, महँगाई और जीवन स्तर में गिरावट आई और सोवियत व्यवस्था में जनता का विश्वास समाप्त हो गया।

Advocated for a strong centralised government and national integration
Promoted Swadeshi (indigenous) economics to build a self-reliant India
Wanted reversal of partition and reunification of India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh (Akhand Bharat)

questions.solution: Yes, the ideology of the Bharatiya Jana Sangh (BJS), founded by Shyama Prasad Mukherjee in 1951, was indeed oriented towards building a progressive and strong India. Four arguments support this view: first, the BJS advocated for 'One Country, One Nation, One Culture', emphasising national unity and integration as the foundation of a strong state. Second, it supported a strong centralised government capable of resisting both external threats and internal fragmentation. Third, it promoted Swadeshi economics — preferring indigenous industries and self-reliance over foreign dependency — which it believed would make India economically powerful. Fourth, the BJS stood for the revocation of Article 370 for Jammu and Kashmir and the concept of Akhand Bharat, reflecting its vision of a territorially and politically unified, strong Indian nation.

questions.text_english: During the decade of 1960, how did the Congress Party resolve the challenge of political succession ? Explain.

key_points: Death of Nehru in 1964 created first succession crisis — resolved by electing Lal Bahadur Shastri
Death of Shastri in 1966 created second crisis — resolved by electing Indira Gandhi as PM
The succession was managed through internal party consensus and the role of the 'Syndicate'
Democratic transfer of power demonstrated Congress's institutional strength

questions.solution: During the 1960s, the Congress Party faced two significant leadership succession crises, both of which it resolved through internal democratic processes. The first crisis came with the death of Jawaharlal Nehru in May 1964. The party resolved it by selecting Lal Bahadur Shastri as Prime Minister through internal consensus among senior party leaders known as the 'Syndicate'. The second crisis occurred when Shastri died unexpectedly in January 1966 after the Tashkent Declaration. This time, the Syndicate, expecting to control a pliable leader, backed Indira Gandhi over Morarji Desai. Indira Gandhi won the leadership contest and became Prime Minister. Both transitions were peaceful and constitutional, demonstrating the Congress party's institutional resilience and its ability to manage succession democratically.

questions.text_english:
Read the passage given below carefully and answer the questions that follow :

On the reform of structures and processes, the biggest discussion has been on the functioning of the Security Council. Related to this has been the demand for an increase in the UN Security Council's permanent and non-permanent membership so that the realities of contemporary world politics are better reflected in the structure of the organisation. In particular, there are proposals to increase membership from Asia, Africa and South America. Beyond this, the US and other Western countries want improvements in the UN's budgetary procedures and its administration.

sub_questions.text: संयुक्त राष्ट्र संघ के किस अंग के पाँच स्थायी सदस्य हैं ?
sub_questions.text_english: Which organ of the United Nations has five permanent members ?
sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Security Council. The UN Security Council has five permanent members (P5): the United States, United Kingdom, France, Russia, and China. These five countries hold veto power. The General Assembly has all member states with equal voting rights but no permanent membership. The Secretariat and the Economic and Social Council do not have a structure of five permanent members.

sub_questions.text_english: Which country contributes the most in the budget of United Nations Organisation ?
sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) America (United States). The United States is the largest single contributor to the United Nations budget, contributing approximately 22% of the regular UN budget and about 27% of the peacekeeping budget. This is why the passage mentions that the US wants reforms in UN budgetary procedures — as the biggest payer, it seeks greater accountability and efficiency in how the money is spent.

sub_questions.text: सुरक्षा परिषद् के अस्थायी सदस्यों की संख्या को किस वर्ष बढ़ाया गया था ?
sub_questions.text_english: In which year was the strength of non-permanent members of Security Council increased ?
sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) 1965. The number of non-permanent members of the UN Security Council was increased from 6 to 10 in 1965, when Article 23 of the UN Charter was amended. This expansion took effect on 1 January 1966, bringing the total membership of the Security Council from 11 to 15.

options.A: सुरक्षा परिषद् समकालीन राजनीतिक वास्तविकताओं की नुमाइंदगी नहीं करती है।
options.B: सुरक्षा परिषद् के फैसलों पर पश्चिमी मूल्यों और हितों की छाप होती है और कुछ शक्तियों का वर्चस्व होता है।
options.C: सुरक्षा परिषद् में समान प्रतिनिधित्व की कमी है।
options.D: सुरक्षा परिषद् के पास शांति स्थापित करने के लिए एक बड़ी सेना है।

options_english.A: The Security Council no longer represents contemporary political realities.
options_english.B: The Security Council's decisions reflect only western values and interests and are dominated by a few powers.

sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (D). The statement that the Security Council has a large army to establish peace is NOT correct. The UN Security Council does not maintain a standing army of its own. It can authorise member states to contribute troops for peacekeeping operations, but these forces are assembled on a case-by-case basis and are not a permanent military force of the Council. Statements (A), (B), and (C) are all valid criticisms raised in debates about UN Security Council reform.

sub_questions.solution: Despite the devastating destruction of Hiroshima and Nagasaki in 1945, Japan emerged as a major global economic power by the 1970s due to four key factors. First, massive American financial and technical assistance during the post-war reconstruction period helped Japan rebuild its industrial base rapidly. Second, Japan's post-war constitution (Article 9) prohibited Japan from maintaining armed forces except for self-defence, which meant the country could direct enormous resources into economic development rather than military expenditure. Third, Japan's highly educated, disciplined, and innovative workforce drove remarkable advances in technology, manufacturing, and productivity, creating globally competitive industries. Fourth, Japan adopted an export-led growth model, specialising in high-quality electronics, automobiles, and precision machinery that captured world markets, generating the capital and expertise needed for sustained economic growth.

sub_questions.solution: China adopted four major policies under Deng Xiaoping from 1978 onwards to accelerate its economic growth. First, China introduced the Open Door Policy, welcoming foreign direct investment and technology transfer from Western nations and multinational corporations, which modernised Chinese industry. Second, Special Economic Zones (SEZs) were established — such as Shenzhen near Hong Kong — where market-friendly regulations attracted large-scale foreign investment and manufacturing, serving as engines of export-led growth. Third, agricultural reforms were introduced, dismantling the collective farming system and allowing farmers to sell surplus produce on the open market, which raised rural incomes and agricultural productivity. Fourth, China gradually privatised state-owned enterprises and opened various sectors to competition while the Communist Party retained political control, creating a unique 'socialist market economy' that delivered rapid industrialisation without the political instability seen in other transitioning economies.

sub_questions.text_english: Highlight any four steps taken by the Government of India to minimize the greenhouse gas emissions.

key_points: National Solar Mission under National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC)
Promotion of renewable energy — wind, solar, hydro power
Energy Efficiency programmes and green building codes
Afforestation drives and protection of forest cover

sub_questions.solution: The Government of India has taken several significant steps to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. First, India launched the National Solar Mission as part of the National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC), with an ambitious target of generating 100 GW of solar power, making India one of the world's largest producers of solar energy. Second, India has massively expanded renewable energy capacity including wind, hydro, and biomass energy, setting a target of achieving 500 GW of non-fossil energy capacity by 2030. Third, India committed at the Paris Climate Agreement (COP21) to reduce the carbon intensity of its GDP by 45% by 2030, and has been pursuing energy efficiency programmes across industries. Fourth, India has implemented large-scale afforestation drives and forest conservation programmes to enhance carbon sinks, including the Green India Mission, which aims to increase forest and tree cover across millions of hectares.

sub_questions.text_english: How does geo-politics of natural resources determine the balance of power in the contemporary world ? Examine.

key_points: Control over oil and gas reserves gives geopolitical leverage — OPEC nations' power
Wars and conflicts over resource-rich regions (Gulf War, Iraq War linked to oil)
Strategic competition for rare earth minerals needed for modern technology
Water scarcity creating international tensions in South Asia and Africa

sub_questions.solution: The geo-politics of natural resources plays a decisive role in shaping the balance of power in the contemporary world. Countries that possess or control large reserves of oil and natural gas wield enormous geopolitical influence — as seen with OPEC nations that can destabilise global economies by manipulating energy prices. Wars and military interventions are frequently linked to resource interests, as demonstrated by the Gulf War (1990) and the Iraq War (2003), both connected to control over West Asian oil. In recent decades, the global competition for rare earth minerals — essential for manufacturing smartphones, electric vehicles, and military technology — has intensified tensions, particularly between the US and China, which controls around 80% of rare earth production. Similarly, growing water scarcity is creating inter-state tensions in South Asia and Africa, where shared river systems become sources of conflict. Thus, the nation or alliance that controls critical natural resources acquires strategic leverage that directly shapes the global balance of power.

sub_questions.text_english: Analyse any three principles of India's foreign policy which you would like to alter in the present international scenario.

key_points: Non-alignment may need updating to strategic partnerships in a bipolar US-China world
Panchsheel's emphasis on non-interference may need revision given cross-border terrorism
Policy of restraint on nuclear weapons may need reassessment given regional threats

sub_questions.solution: Three principles of India's foreign policy that may need reconsideration in the contemporary international scenario are as follows. First, the principle of Non-Alignment, while historically valuable in avoiding Cold War power blocs, may need updating in today's world dominated by US-China rivalry, where India may benefit more from clear strategic alliances than from studied neutrality. Second, the Panchsheel principle of strict non-interference in other nations' internal affairs may need recalibration given that cross-border terrorism sponsored by state actors like Pakistan directly threatens Indian security, making a stronger, more interventionist approach necessary. Third, India's policy of a minimum credible nuclear deterrent may need reassessment given the rapid expansion of China's nuclear arsenal and Pakistan's growing capabilities — India might need to reconsider the sufficiency of its current nuclear posture to maintain genuine deterrence.

sub_questions.text: "भारत की परमाणु नीति सामरिक स्वायत्तता और वैश्विक निःशस्त्रीकरण के प्रति प्रतिबद्धता का मिश्रण है।" किन्हीं तीन उचित तर्कों सहित कथन को न्यायोचित ठहराइये।
sub_questions.text_english: "India's nuclear policy is a blend of strategic autonomy and a commitment to global disarmament." Justify the statement with any three suitable arguments.

key_points: India maintains No First Use (NFU) policy showing restraint and commitment to peace
India refused to sign NPT as discriminatory but supports universal disarmament
India's nuclear doctrine focuses on minimum credible deterrence, not arms race

sub_questions.solution: India's nuclear policy is indeed a blend of strategic autonomy and commitment to global disarmament, as demonstrated by three key arguments. First, India maintains a No First Use (NFU) policy, pledging never to use nuclear weapons first against any nation — this reflects a commitment to peace and restraint even while retaining nuclear capability as a deterrent against threats. Second, India refused to sign the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) as it considers it discriminatory — it allows existing nuclear powers to retain their weapons while preventing others from developing them. However, India has consistently supported the goal of universal, complete, and verifiable nuclear disarmament under international supervision, as articulated in the Rajiv Gandhi Plan (1988). Third, India follows a doctrine of minimum credible deterrence, maintaining only enough nuclear capability to deter adversaries rather than engaging in an arms buildup, which underlines its strategic autonomy while remaining aligned with the broader goal of a nuclear-free world.

sub_questions.text_english: How did Princely states posed a threat to the National Security of India ? Explain.

key_points: Over 565 princely states had the right to remain independent — risked fragmentation of India
Hyderabad's Nizam refused to accede and had to be integrated through 'Police Action'
Junagarh's Nawab declared accession to Pakistan despite majority Hindu population
Kashmir's ambiguity led to the first India-Pakistan war

sub_questions.solution: At the time of independence in 1947, India had over 565 princely states that were technically free to remain independent or join either India or Pakistan. This created three major threats to India's national unity and security. First, the possibility of fragmentation was real — had many states chosen independence, India would have been carved into hundreds of small, unviable units, fundamentally undermining national unity. Second, the Nizam of Hyderabad refused to accede to India, instead seeking independence and even approaching the UN, which threatened to leave a large hostile state in the heart of India. The situation was resolved only through the military 'Police Action' (Operation Polo) in September 1948. Third, the ambiguous position of Kashmir — whose Maharaja initially wanted independence — created the biggest security crisis when Pakistani-backed tribal forces invaded, leading to the first India-Pakistan war and leaving a territorial dispute that continues to destabilise the region even today.

sub_questions.text: भारत के विभाजन के दौरान सामने आई किन्हीं चार समस्याओं की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain any four problems faced during the process of partition of India.

key_points: Massive communal violence and riots killing hundreds of thousands
Unprecedented refugee crisis with 1.5 crore people displaced
Division of civil services, military, and assets between India and Pakistan
Drawing of borders (Radcliffe Line) causing immense disruption to communities

sub_questions.solution: The partition of India in August 1947 was accompanied by four devastating problems. First, unprecedented communal violence erupted across Punjab and Bengal, with Hindus, Muslims, and Sikhs killing each other in horrifying numbers — estimates of deaths range from 2 to 5 lakh people — making it one of history's most violent mass displacements. Second, the partition triggered the largest refugee crisis in human history, with approximately 1.5 crore people displaced — Hindus and Sikhs fleeing to India and Muslims fleeing to Pakistan — causing immense human suffering and logistical challenges for both new governments. Third, the administrative division was highly complex — civil services, military forces, financial assets, and government records had to be divided between two countries in a matter of weeks, creating enormous institutional chaos. Fourth, the drawing of the Radcliffe Line to demarcate borders cut through communities, families, irrigated farmlands, and railway networks, leaving many people stranded on the wrong side of the border and creating lasting bitterness.
